name: Progressive Familial Intrahepatic Cholestasis Type 5

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic variants in the NR1H4 gene
Clinical and biochemical evidence of intrahepatic cholestasis with elevated serum bile acids
Exclusion of other causes of cholestasis including biliary atresia and other PFIC types
Liver biopsy showing canalicular cholestasis with absence or reduction of bile salt export pump (BSEP) expression

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical cholestasis with genetic confirmation of NR1H4 mutation and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on genetic testing due to overlapping clinical features with other PFIC types.

pathognomonic.notes: Intense itching often refractory to standard treatments
searchTerms: itching due to liver bile problems

pathognomonic.notes: Persistent elevation of serum bile acids and conjugated hyperbilirubinemia
searchTerms: worsening bile flow blockage inside liver

pathognomonic.symptomName: Neonatal or early infancy onset jaundice
pathognomonic.notes: Jaundice appearing within first months of life
searchTerms: jaundice starting in newborn or early infancy

common.notes: Poor weight gain and growth delay
Deficiencies of vitamins A, D, E, and K due to malabsorption
searchTerms: lack of vitamins A, D, E, K

common.notes: Fatty stools secondary to impaired bile flow

occasional.notes: Cholesterol deposits in skin due to impaired bile acid metabolism
Bleeding tendency due to vitamin K deficiency

rare.notes: Rare malignant transformation in advanced disease

rare.symptomName: Neurological complications secondary to vitamin E deficiency
searchTerms: neurological problems from vitamin E deficiency
nerve issues due to low vitamin E
cognitive and motor symptoms from vitamin E lack

rare.notes: End-stage liver disease due to chronic cholestasis

laboratory: Prolonged prothrombin time due to vitamin K deficiency
imaging: Ultrasound showing hepatomegaly and absence of biliary obstruction
other: Liver biopsy showing canalicular cholestasis and reduced BSEP expression

distinguishingFeatures: Different bile salt export pump involvement
Earlier onset with low GGT levels

redFlags: Severe refractory pruritus unresponsive to medical therapy
Development of coagulopathy or bleeding diathesis
references: Jansen PLM, et al. Progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis: diagnosis, management, and treatment. Hepatology. 2020.
Orphanet: Progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis type 5. ORPHA:480476.
